affectedPublicSurfaces: demo.app-juli.com run surfaces (apps/demo — landing, Decisions, staged run view, option picker)
the release workflow's browser suite (release.yml apps/demo E2E)

candidateVerificationJourney.restrictedRoute: The suite runs against the built candidate before cutover, matching how the existing apps/demo E2E already runs in release.yml. Deterministic because it is replay — no model, no marketplace, no external network
candidateVerificationJourney.notes: Issue's own Release evidence section, transcribed verbatim; no additional surfaces inferred. The journey is replay-driven, so it performs no marketplace write and needs no synthetic shop.

journeys.name: replay-journey-end-to-end
assertions: Dùng thử Demo → Decisions → approve → staged run view → stages advance → pick an option → confirm → completion
the journey asserts the confirmation request the client SENT, so a UI that looks right while sending the wrong option fails
deterministic across ten consecutive runs — flakiness is a failure, not a retry

journeys.name: forced-disconnect-reconnect-is-gapless
assertions: a forced mid-run disconnect and reconnect is part of the journey
the post-reconnect view state equals the uninterrupted one
the reconnect renders as a stream condition, never as a run failure

journeys.name: fixture-absence-fails-loudly
assertions: the journey FAILS rather than skips when the scenario fixture is missing from the built artifact
a rolled-back build lacking the run route makes the suite fail rather than pass, so a bad rollback is visible

staticAssetChecks.notes: Issue text: 'the scenario fixtures and the new routes must be present in the artifact the suite runs against — assert, do not assume.' Read the built artifact, not the source tree.

migrationCompatibility.notes: Issue text: 'No migration.' A CI journey, dictionary entries and documentation truthfulness — no database schema, no persisted-shape change.

rollbackAssertion.notes: Issue text: 'assert the suite fails rather than passes against a rolled-back build that lacks the run route, so a bad rollback is visible.' A rollback that silently passes the suite is the failure mode this assertion exists to catch.

doNotInfer: release evidence fields beyond what the issue's Release evidence (ADR-035) section states
a retry or rerun wrapper around the replay journey — flakiness across ten consecutive runs is specified as a failure, not something to paper over
a journey that skips when the scenario fixture is absent; it must fail loudly
